title: Babies differ in inborn temperament
summary: OpenStax says temperament is inborn, and it contrasts an easy pattern of positive emotion and adaptability with a difficult pattern of negative emotion and harder adjustment.
body: OpenStax Psychology defines temperament as innate traits that influence how a person thinks, behaves, and reacts to the environment. Children described as easy show positive emotions, adapt well to change, and can regulate their emotions. Children described as difficult show negative emotions and have difficulty adapting and regulating emotion. The page says difficult children are much more likely to challenge caregivers, citing Thomas, 1984, which was not opened here. It also says it is possible that easy children draw warmer care and that irritable children evoke irritation. That possibility is the textbook's suggestion, not a rule that a baby's style causes a caregiver's response.
